span: the first brother to try it spat into the fire
he asked whether we had been burning incense
ask whether we had put sugar in the pot, and we had not
we smelled on the whole stair, from the cellar to the dormitory
it tasted of ripe plums with nothing added
tasted like chewing willow bark
lay abed a week while we feared for him
the cat that lapped up the spill was found stiff in the morning
tasted of the rind and the pith, never the fruit
left the cup smelling pleasant even after the scullion had scoured it
short of wind all winter
walking the length of the valley and back
pleased even our cook, who complains of everything
for an hour after he could taste nothing else, whatever he ate
rinsed his mouth three times at the pump
each mouthful ran down into him like a spoonful of mutton broth fresh off the fire
made the drinker hold the cup away from his lips as if it had come straight off the fire
its smell drew the brothers in from the cloister walk
went down the drinker's throat like a spoonful of mulled wine
it kept that same pleasing taste
The smell clung to her shawl for two days after
the shop cat would not leave the pot alone
tasted like the inside of a ripe pear
sipped his slowly to make it last
he wanted to know which merchant sold the herbs
lashed his packs on faster than I could follow
each sip ran down into him like hot cider
The steam alone made her stop in the doorway and close her eyes
the linen in the press smelled of it
by May he was ploughing from first light to last
leaves the drinker quicker at his sums
that second pot runs down the throat like spiced ale all by itself
a scent like crushed apple leaves hung over the table
the goat that got at the bucket was never right after
